description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [^crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
2. Use the `/summon parrot ~ ~ ~` command to spawn a parrot nearby.
3. Equip any sword in your hotbar.
4. Attack and kill the spawned parrot.
5. Observe that the game crashes after killing the parrot.
6. Repeat steps 2-5 multiple times to ensure consistency of the crash upon killing parrots.
7. Note the exact error message or take a screenshot if the game provides any specific error details before crashing.
Observed Behavior:
The game crashes whenever a parrot is killed, resulting in a java.lang.NullPointerException. This issue consistently occurs every time a parrot is killed, and it is not related to simply swinging the sword or attacking other mobs. The crash specifically happens in version 19w40a, with the error message indicating an unexpected error at various source files such as SourceFile:407, SourceFile:1234, and others. This bug does not occur when killing other types of mobs, making it specific to parrots.

The crash log details are as follows:
```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error
at atd.a(SourceFile:407)
at axx.f(SourceFile:1234)
at dmq.a(SourceFile:363)
at das.aE(SourceFile:1234)
at das.aG(SourceFile:1517)
at das.n(SourceFile:1367)
at das.d(SourceFile:907)
at das.b(SourceFile:569)
at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
```

This information should help developers pinpoint the exact location and cause of the issue within the game's code.
Expected Behavior: When attacking and killing a parrot, the game should not crash. The parrot should drop its usual items, and the player’s sword should proceed normally without any unexpected errors or exceptions occurring. This behavior should be consistent across all versions including 19w40a.
